passages.title: A Life-Changing Summer in Peru
passages.text: Last summer, I decided to do something completely different. Instead of spending my holidays at home, I signed up for a volunteer program in a small village in the Peruvian Andes. I had always wanted to travel, but I wanted to do more than just visit tourist sites; I wanted to make a real difference. When I arrived, I was surprised by how different everything was. The air was thin, the mountains were breathtaking, and the local community was incredibly welcoming. My main job was to help build a new classroom for the primary school. I had never held a hammer or painted a wall before, but the local builders were very patient with me. They taught me how to mix cement and how to work as part of a team. It was hard physical work, especially in the heat, but I felt a great sense of achievement every evening. In the afternoons, I helped the children with their English homework. They were so eager to learn, and we often spent hours laughing as we tried to communicate through gestures and simple words. Living without electricity and limited internet access was a challenge at first. I missed my friends and the comforts of home, but as the weeks passed, I realized that I didn't need those things to be happy. I learned to appreciate the simple things, like a shared meal or a beautiful sunset over the peaks. This experience changed my perspective on life. I realized that we don't need much to be happy, and that helping others is one of the most rewarding things you can do. I returned home with a new sense of purpose and a promise to myself that I would continue volunteering in the future. I have already started looking for local opportunities in my own city.

questions.question: Why did the writer choose to volunteer in Peru?
questions.explanation: The writer wanted to do something meaningful rather than just being a tourist.
options: a) To improve his Spanish language skills.
b) To escape the cold weather at home.
c) To contribute to something meaningful.
d) To learn how to build houses professionally.

questions.question: How did the writer feel about the building work?
questions.explanation: The writer mentions feeling a great sense of achievement despite the hard work.
options: a) He found it too difficult to continue.
b) He felt proud of what he accomplished.
c) He was disappointed by the lack of tools.
d) He preferred teaching children to building.

questions.question: What does the writer say about the lack of technology?
questions.explanation: He says it was a challenge at first, but he eventually realized he didn't need those things to be happy.
options: a) It was difficult initially but became easier.
b) It made him feel very lonely.
c) It prevented him from learning the local language.
d) It was the main reason he wanted to leave.

questions.question: What is the writer's main conclusion after the trip?
questions.explanation: He says he returned with a new sense of purpose and intends to keep volunteering.
options: a) He wants to move to Peru permanently.
b) He regrets not spending more time at home.
c) He thinks volunteering is only for young people.
d) He plans to continue helping others in the future.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the writer's attitude?
questions.explanation: The writer is positive and reflective about his growth through volunteering.
options: a) He is critical of the living conditions in the village.
b) He is surprised that he survived the trip.
c) He is grateful for the experience and what he learned.
d) He is worried that he won't find work at home.
